newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: EMCO says to remove spikes from final power prices.
newsitem.headline: EMCO says to remove spikes from final power prices.

text.p: Electricity Market Company Ltd (EMCO) said on Tuesday that final wholesale electricity prices for October would be adjusted to remove some of the price spikes that had appeared in provisional prices.

The Market Surveillance Committee, after considering a preliminary EMCO report, called for a full investigation of the price spikes caused when the amount of electricity offered by generators was found to be inconsistent with what was actually provided.
The EMCO report said one of the main reasons for the inconsistencies centred on the "ramp rate" at which some generation plants, especially large thermal units, can increase and decrease production.
"If one of the large thermal units cannot increase output quickly enough to meet an increase in demand, additional generation must be found from other, generally more expensive, sources," EMCO said.
As an interim measure, the Market Surveillance Committee had instructed that ramp rates should be removed from final prices, Prices may be reviewed again after its investigation.

This would mean average prices for some days in October would fall by up to 18 percent, and others would rise by less than one percent, but not all provisional prices published for the month would be affected, EMCO said.
"Over the past few days, the running of expensive generation plant in the North Island has resulted in provisional prices being higher than expected. This is also being investigated," EMCO said.
